lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
Date of birth: 5 Feb 1998 | Nationality: Singaporean
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality.
items.because: These personal details are unrelated to assessing qualifications and are conventionally left off.

items.says: Experience should appear before Education.
items.because: Several years of post-degree experience make the work history more relevant to lead with.

items.says: The duties give no outcome for members.
The tournament bullet does not identify your specific responsibility or its result.
items.because: “Helped the pro shop run” could mean general support, and no outcome shows what the work contributed.

items.says: The 40% efficiency gain has no baseline or comparison period.
items.because: Without the prior close time or effort, the improvement is harder to interpret and less credible.

items.says: The repeated “by” makes the relationship between the gain and the method clunky.
The template bullet does not say what standardizing criteria enabled.
The final clause is wordy.
items.because: The shared template already conveys standardization.

items.says: The board-pack bullet names the deliverable but not its consequence.
“Each line more than 5% off budget” awkwardly describes the items covered.
Free cash flow to equity is paired with the wrong discount rate.
items.because: FCFE is ordinarily discounted at the cost of equity, while WACC is used for free cash flow to the firm.

items.says: The acquisition valuation has no amount or range.
items.because: The reader cannot see the scale or result of the valuation work.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins cannot calculate a group EBITDA margin.
items.because: Group margin is total group EBITDA divided by total group revenue, or a revenue-weighted average of unit margins.

items.says: The reporting bullet does not say what your work contributed or enabled.
The strongest Stonebridge bullet should appear first.
“Letting treasury pay down” is informal and makes your contribution less direct.
The underwriting bullet does not identify the analysis or decision criterion used.
items.because: The reader cannot see the credit-analysis skill behind the decisions.

items.says: The declined-application analysis and its results should lead the entry.
The first-person pronoun “my” does not belong in the bullet.
“Writes” is present tense although the role ended in December 2022.
items.because: The role dates and other bullets describe completed work.

items.says: “From 7 to 1 a year” is awkward and makes the annual measure harder to scan.
The market-price comparison does not say whether the valuation was above or below the price or when it was made.
The sensitivity scenario omits the direction, starting rate, and unit of the discount-rate change.
items.because: The reader cannot tell which assumption produced each share value or interpret “one point.”

items.says: “Which used it” could refer to either the model or the note.
The FP&A bullet does not identify a specific task or action.
items.because: The broad wording frames the work as assistance, so the reader cannot picture the work or recognize the skill used.

items.says: The FP&A bullet gives no outcome of the work.
The performance-report bullet should lead the entry.
The forecast bullet does not explain how its error figure was calculated or compared.
items.because: Without that information, “about 4%” is hard to interpret and the accuracy claim is less credible.

items.says: The forecast outcomes would be easier to scan before the setup.
items.because: Accuracy and debt repayment are the bullet’s most concrete parts.

items.says: The cash-forecast bullet repeats an achievement attributed to the later Stonebridge role and does not fit the fund entry.
items.because: The distinctive forecast, error, and debt-repayment results match the Stonebridge bullet, casting doubt on which role they belong to.
